mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by ≥1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines of 1% or more.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.5% month-over-month signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with falling inflation, which historically has been associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to rate-cut expectations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by more than -0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household demand, which boosts consumption and investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST increase month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) continues to grow signals a shift from low-quality to high-quality job creation, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved labor market balance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE exceeds 4% and PAYEMS increases simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) alongside flat or declining personal consumption expenditures (implied by GDPC1) signals a precautionary savings regime, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to weak consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises for three consecutive months AND GDPC1 is flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS rises for three months and GDPC1 is flat or declines.
